1: Eternal Life Has Appeared in Christ
“Certainties of the Word of Life, Part 1”
Says John begins with Jesus Christ, who was from the beginning and whom the apostles heard, saw and touched, so that their witness rests on real, physical experience.
John begins with the center of relationship: Jesus Christ

For not only did they see the Lord with their physical eyes like the others, but they also perceived His divine power with their spiritual eyes. Especially those who saw Him transfigured on the mount, among whom was John himself.
2: Daily Study Bible · The Pastor’s Aim · vv.1–4

Barclay says the pastor opens by stating his aim, his right to speak as one who saw and heard, and his message, which is the word of life, so that his readers may share the fellowship and have their joy completed.
It was with the Father in eternal divinity, and appeared in time to the world in humanity.
3: Eternal Life Has Appeared in Christ
Fellowship with the Father and the Son
Reads John’s declaration as an invitation to share the fellowship the apostles have with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.

Blessed John clearly shows that anyone who desires to have fellowship with God must first be united with the fellowship of the Church, learn that faith, and be imbued with its sacraments, which the disciples received from the Truth dwelling in the flesh itself.
4: The joy of teachers is made complete when, through preaching, they lead many to the fellowship of the holy Church, and to the fellowship of God the Father and his Son Jesus Christ, through whom the Church is strengthened and grows.
5: Daily Study Bible · God Is Light · v.5

Barclay says that to call God light is to speak of his splendour, his self-revealing nature, his purity, his guidance and his power to show up what is hidden, and he takes darkness as the Christless life and all that is hostile to God.
Says John claims authority for this message, which is God’s own word about himself: God is light and in him is no darkness at all.
Sin and the nature of God

By this statement, blessed John both shows the excellence of divine purity, which we are also commanded to imitate, saying: Be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy (Leviticus XIX); and he refutes the insane doctrine of the Manicheans, who said that the nature of God was conquered and corrupted by the prince of darkness in war.
6: The Child of Light Walking in Light
Daily Study Bible · The Necessity of Walking in the Light · vv.6–7

Barclay says John answers those who claimed to be so advanced that sin no longer mattered, insisting that fellowship with the God who is light means walking in the light, and that hatred toward anyone shows love for God is not real.

He names darkness, sins, heresies, and hatreds. Therefore, the mere confession of faith alone is not sufficient for salvation, to which the testimony of good works is lacking. But neither does the rectitude of works without the simplicity of faith and love profit.
7: Let Us Walk in the Light of God
Walking in the Light and Washed in the Blood
Takes walking in the light as a generally obedient life that does not harbor known sin, with fellowship and the cleansing blood of Jesus as the blessing.
The blessing of walking in the light

For indeed, the sacrament of the Lord's passion both alleviated all past sins for us in baptism and forgives whatever we commit after baptism due to daily frailty, by the grace of the same our Redeemer.
8: “Total Forgiveness and the Confession of Sin”
This sentence avails against the heresy of Pelagius, which claimed that all infants are born without sin and that the elect in this life can progress to such an extent as to be without sin.
9: Let Us Walk in the Light of God
“Total Forgiveness and the Confession of Sin”
Daily Study Bible · The Sinner’s Self-Deception · vv.8–10

Barclay describes two mistaken ways of thought, the person who denies responsibility for sin and the person who claims never to have sinned, and says that only humble confession opens the door to forgiveness because God, being righteous, keeps his word.
Because we cannot be without sin in this life, the first hope of salvation is confession, and no one should consider themselves just or lift up their neck before the eyes of God.
10: “Total Forgiveness and the Confession of Sin”
For he himself said through a man filled with his Spirit: There is no just man on earth who does good and does not sin (Ecclesiastes 7).

1: Jesus Christ Is an Advocate for Sinners
Says John writes so that believers will not sin, though the end of chapter 1 made plain that sin happens and that confessed sin is always forgiven.
A purpose of John in writing this letter: that you may not sin
See how John himself maintains the humility he teaches; surely he was a righteous and great man, who drank the secrets of mysteries from the Lord's breast.
2: Daily Study Bible · A Pastor’s Concern · vv.1–2
Barclay notes John’s tenderness as perhaps the last man alive who had walked with Jesus, and calls Jesus the Paraclete who pleads our cause and the propitiation for our sins.
He who intercedes for us with the Father through his humanity, also propitiates for us with the Father through his divinity.
3: Obedience Confirms Our Standing in God
Daily Study Bible · The True Knowledge of God · vv.3–6
Barclay says the ancient world also sought to know God, but Christianity differs by joining knowledge to obedience, so that intellectual effort and emotional experience must issue in moral action.
Which commandments he means, he explains subsequently, that is, love.
4: Says the evidence that we know God is keeping his commandments, and that whoever claims to abide in him ought to walk as he walked.
Christ is called the truth: “I am” (He says) “the way, the truth, and the life” (John XIV). Therefore, it is futile for us to boast about knowing Him when we do not keep His commandments.
5: Obedience Confirms Our Standing in God
Daily Study Bible · The True Knowledge of God · vv.3–6
Barclay says the ancient world also sought to know God, but Christianity differs by joining knowledge to obedience, so that intellectual effort and emotional experience must issue in moral action.

Therefore, truly the one who keeps God's commandments and proves by his love has true knowledge of God. For to know God is to love Him. For whoever does not love Him clearly shows that he does not know how lovable He is.
6: Says the evidence that we know God is keeping his commandments, and that whoever claims to abide in him ought to walk as he walked.
Therefore, it is said that one who abides in God should also direct the paths of their own life according to Him.
7: The One Who Loves Lives in Light
Daily Study Bible · The Commandment Which Is Old and New · vv.7–8

Barclay hears warm affection in the word beloved, and says the commandment of love is old because it was there from the beginning and new because the darkness is passing, since the coming of Christ means the reign of love.
The same love is also an old commandment, for it has been recommended from the beginning, and it is a new commandment because, with the darkness cast out, it infuses the desire for new light.
8: Says the commandment of love is both old and new, and that a person who claims to be in the light yet hates his brother is still in darkness.
Behold here is the new, for darkness pertains to the old man and the light truly to the new man.
9: The One Who Loves Lives in Light
Daily Study Bible · Love and Hate, and Light and Dark · vv.9–11
Barclay says John sees personal relationships in black and white, with no neutrality, so that love lets a person walk in the light while hatred leaves him in the dark even if he does not realise it.
The Lord has commanded to love enemies; therefore, he who says he is a Christian and hates his brother is still in sins.
10: Says the commandment of love is both old and new, and that a person who claims to be in the light yet hates his brother is still in darkness.

That is, no offense; for he who loves his brother endures all things for the unity of unity. For much peace is for those who love your name (Psalm CXVIII), that is, charity, and there is no stumbling for them (Ibid.).
11: The One Who Loves Lives in Light
Daily Study Bible · Love and Hate, and Light and Dark · vv.9–11
Barclay says John sees personal relationships in black and white, with no neutrality, so that love lets a person walk in the light while hatred leaves him in the dark even if he does not realise it.

For he, ignorant, falls into hell, blind and unaware, withdrawing from the light of Christ who warns and says: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life” (John VIII).
12: A Sermon to the Lord’s Little Children
Says each believer begins as a little child, and at that stage it is enough to be amazed that sins are forgiven for his name’s sake.
Little children, who have their sins forgiven
He glorifies all his hearers, whom he had preceded in Christ, with the name of children, because, having been reborn of water and the Spirit, they had received the remission of sins.
13: He calls fathers not by age, but by greater wisdom and maturity. For venerable old age is not counted by long duration nor by the number of years.
14: Says the repetition shows emphasis, and that the young men’s victory comes through the strength of God’s word abiding in them.
Consider again and again that you are young men, fight so that you may conquer, conquer so that you may be crowned. Be humble, lest you fall in battle.
15: Let no one deceive himself. One heart does not accommodate two loves so opposed to each other.
16: Daily Study Bible · Rivals for the Human Heart · vv.15–17

Barclay sets John’s warning against the world beside the ancient picture of life as a battle between light and dark, and says the man of the world is doomed to disappointment while the man of God has given himself to what lasts for ever.
Says the world expresses itself through the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes and the pride of life.

Therefore, all that is in the world, that is, all lovers of the world, have nothing but the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life. By these names of vices, he comprehends all kinds of vices.
17: The world will pass away, when on the day of judgment it will be transformed by fire into a better form, so that there will be a new heaven and a new earth. And its desire will pass away, because the time for a life of luxury, or for any sin, will be no more.
18: Daily Study Bible · The Time of the Last Hour · v.18

Barclay traces how the phrase the last hour grew in meaning through the Old Testament, then turns to the Antichrist and the battle of the mind, and says the Church must learn to counter evil ideas spread through the media.
Says John writes in the last hour, when many antichrists have come, and that those who left the fellowship showed they were never really of it.
The danger of false religion: the spirit of Antichrist

He calls heretics Antichrists; but also those who, by perverse actions, destroy the Catholic faith which they profess, are rightly called Antichrists, that is, contrary to Christ; who all bear witness to that great Antichrist who will come at the end of the age, as to their head.
19: Daily Study Bible · The Sifting of the Church · vv.19–21
Barclay reads the departure of the false teachers as a sifting that showed they never belonged, and says the readers already have enough light to walk by if they would only use it.

Therefore, it must be seen that many who are not of us receive the sacraments of Christ with us. But temptation proves that they are not of us, for when temptation comes to them, like the wind they fly away, because they were not the grain.
20: Let What You Heard from the Beginning Abide in You
Daily Study Bible · The Sifting of the Church · vv.19–21
Barclay reads the departure of the false teachers as a sifting that showed they never belonged, and says the readers already have enough light to walk by if they would only use it.
Says believers have an anointing from the Holy One, and that the mark of the antichrist is denying that Jesus is the Christ, which denies the Father and the Son.

The spiritual anointing is the Holy Spirit, whose sacrament is in the visible anointing. He says that all who have this anointing of Christ have the ability to discern the good and the evil, and that there is no need for them to be taught those things which the anointing itself teaches.
21: Daily Study Bible · The Sifting of the Church · vv.19–21
Barclay reads the departure of the false teachers as a sifting that showed they never belonged, and says the readers already have enough light to walk by if they would only use it.
For you know the truth of faith and life taught by the anointing of the Spirit, and you do not need to be taught, except that you should persist in what you have begun.
22: Let What You Heard from the Beginning Abide in You
Says believers have an anointing from the Holy One, and that the mark of the antichrist is denying that Jesus is the Christ, which denies the Father and the Son.

He had foretold that every lie is not from the truth, but since there are many kinds of lies that are not at all similar, now he sets forth the lie of denial of Christ as singular because this is such a heinous and abominable lie that in comparison to it, other lies either seem small or nonexistent.
23: Daily Study Bible · The Master Lie · vv.22–23

Barclay calls the denial that Jesus is the Anointed One the master lie, and says John rejects the claim that the false teachers still shared the same belief about God, since no one who denies the Son can have the Father.

Here he seeks the confession of the heart, the voice, and the work, as Paul sought when he said: And no one can say “Jesus is Lord” except by the Holy Spirit; which is openly to say: No one can, unless by the grace of the Holy Spirit granted, serve the Lord Christ with perfect profession and action.
24: Let What You Heard from the Beginning Abide in You
Says we guard against the spirit of antichrist by abiding in the original, core Christian message and so in the Son and the Father.
Preserving relationship: abiding in the true Christian message and in God

He says, follow with all your heart that faith, those doctrines which you have received from the voice of the apostles from the earliest times of the nascent Church. For these alone are what make you partakers of divine grace.
25: Says the promise that comes with abiding is eternal life, which is more than mere immortality.
The blessing of abiding in the truth and in God: eternal life
Let the remembrance of the promised reward make you perseverant in your work.
26: Let What You Heard from the Beginning Abide in You

By deceivers whom he names, not only are heretics to be understood, who seek to turn away from the faith by wicked doctrine, but also those who, by allurements or by adversities of the world, detract the minds of the weak from the promise of eternal life, either by enticing them evilly or by frightening them.
27: Daily Study Bible · The Universal Privilege · vv.24–29
Barclay says John pleads with his people to abide in what they learned, and that the profession a person makes will always be proved or disproved by his practice of righteousness.
Says John knew there was deception among the early Christians, and that the anointing the believer has received from God abides and teaches.
Our protection against deception: the anointing
Do not be carried away by various and strange doctrines. In the faith and the tradition which he himself taught, abide in him.
28: Preparation for the Coming of the Lord

Whoever remains in the Lord amidst the persecutions of the unbelievers, amidst the mockeries of carnal neighbors, has confidence in his coming, knowing that the patience of the poor will not perish at the end.
29: The beginning of our righteousness is the confession of sins. You have begun not to defend your sin; you have already started righteousness. It will be perfected in you when you will be pleased to do nothing else.

1: The Depth of Christ’s Love: Its Lavish Benefits
“And We Are”: A Jewel from the Revised Version
Daily Study Bible · Remember the Privileges of the Christian Life · vv.1–2
Barclay asks the readers to remember the privilege of being called children of God and the possibility of rising higher still, ending on the Christian hope of seeing God.
For this reason, the world does not know us, because it did not know Him. In this place, he calls the lovers of the world.
2: Daily Study Bible · Remember the Privileges of the Christian Life · vv.1–2
Barclay asks the readers to remember the privilege of being called children of God and the possibility of rising higher still, ending on the Christian hope of seeing God.
Says our present standing as children of God is plain, while our future destiny is not yet fully revealed.
And Paul says: For you are dead, and your life is hidden with Christ in God (Colossians III).
3: Many say they have the hope of heavenly life in Christ, but they make this confession void by living negligently.
4: The Son of God Appeared to Destroy the Works of the Devil
Let no one say: sin is one thing, lawlessness another. Let no one say: I am a sinner but not lawless. For everyone who commits sin also practices lawlessness, because sin is lawlessness.
5: The Son of God Appeared to Destroy the Works of the Devil
Defines sin at its root as lawlessness, a disregard for the Lawmaker, and says Jesus appeared to take away our sins.
The nature of sin and Jesus’ work in removing our sin
John the Baptist also bore witness to this about the Lord, saying: Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world. The Lord was able to take away sins because there was no sin in Him.
6: Says the verb tense John uses means that one who abides in Jesus does not live a lifestyle of habitual sin.
Abiding in sin or abiding in God
To the extent he remains in Him, to that extent he does not sin.
7: The Son of God Appeared to Destroy the Works of the Devil
Daily Study Bible · The Obligation of Purity · vv.3–8
Barclay says a great aim helps a man resist temptation, and reads the passage as aimed at Gnostic teachers who excused sin, since the Son of God appeared to destroy the works of the devil.
For we also, according to our measure, if we were not in some way like Him, would by no means be called similar.
8: The Works of the Devil Destroyed
Daily Study Bible · The Obligation of Purity · vv.3–8
Barclay says a great aim helps a man resist temptation, and reads the passage as aimed at Gnostic teachers who excused sin, since the Son of God appeared to destroy the works of the devil.

Not deriving the origin of the flesh from the devil, as the Manichean impiously believes of all men, but taking the imitation or suggestion of sinning from him, in the same way that we become children of Abraham by imitating the faith of Abraham.
9: Daily Study Bible · The Man Who Is Born of God · v.9
Barclay offers two readings of the seed of God and concludes that John is not saying the man who abides in God cannot sin, but that he cannot go on being a deliberate sinner.
Says people settled in habitual sin are of the devil, and that Jesus came to destroy the devil’s works and free us from bondage to him.
The root of sin and the root of righteousness

However, this is not said of every sin: for if we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves (1 John 1), but of the violation of charity, which one who has the seed of God, that is, the word of God, by which he is reborn, cannot commit within himself.
10: The Son of God Appeared to Destroy the Works of the Devil
Therefore, only love distinguishes between the children of God and the children of the devil. Those who have charity are born of God. Those who do not have it are not born of God.
11: Says the basic Christian message has not changed since the beginning, and that John is remembering Jesus’ command to love one another.
The need to love one another
The Lord saying: This is my commandment, that you love one another (John XV).
12: Presents Cain as the negative example, who was not right with God and who hated his brother.

He explains how Cain was of the evil one because he himself had evil deeds. Therefore, where there is envy, brotherly love cannot exist; but the sin of the evil one, that is, the devil, is in such a heart, for the devil also cast out man through envy.
13: Daily Study Bible · The Marks of the Children of God · vv.10–18
Barclay says life reveals the children of God as fruit reveals a tree, explains the world’s resentment of the Christian way, and presses for love in deed and truth rather than in talk.
Says we should not be surprised when the world hates us but should be surprised by hatred inside the body of Christ, and that a believer can know he has passed from death to life.
Love as the evidence of the new birth
He calls those who love the world worldly. Nor should it be wondered that those who love the world cannot love a brother separated from the love of the world and intent only on heavenly desires.
14: Let no one falsely exalt himself over virtues, let no one measure the poverty of his own strength beyond measure: it gives open judgment, whoever is full of fraternal love, that he belongs to the lot of the elect, because he has earned a portion in the land of the living.
15: Daily Study Bible · The Marks of the Children of God · vv.10–18
Barclay says life reveals the children of God as fruit reveals a tree, explains the world’s resentment of the Christian way, and presses for love in deed and truth rather than in talk.
If anyone despised brotherly hatred, would he also despise murder in his heart? He does not move his hands to kill a man, yet he is already considered a murderer by God.
16: Says how we define love matters, and starts from the Greek words for love to show what love is and how it shows in our life.
The objective reality of love and how it shows in our life
What kind of perfect love ought to be in us, we have learned from the example of the Lord's passion. For no one has greater love than this, that one lays down his life for his friends (John XV).
17: Daily Study Bible · The Marks of the Children of God · vv.10–18
Barclay says life reveals the children of God as fruit reveals a tree, explains the world’s resentment of the Christian way, and presses for love in deed and truth rather than in talk.

Behold where love begins. If you are not yet fit to die for your brother, be at least fit to give from your possessions to your brother. For if you do not sympathize with your brother suffering hardship, indeed the love of the Father, from whom both of you were reborn, does not abide in you.
18: Says John will not allow love to be only talk, and that if a believer can meet a brother’s need and does nothing, the love of God does not abide in him.
What it means to love in real life

Namely, in deed, so that when a brother or sister is naked and in need of daily food, we give them what is necessary for the body. Similarly, when we see them lacking in spiritual gifts, let us provide to their need what we can.
19: Daily Study Bible · The Only Test · vv.19–24
Barclay says doubts come to every sensitive heart and John’s test is simple, namely love, and that the commands to believe and to love belong together and cannot be separated.
That is, when we perform acts of piety in truth, it is evident that we are of the truth, which is God, just as we imitate His perfection according to our capacity.
20: Daily Study Bible · The Only Test · vv.19–24
Barclay says doubts come to every sensitive heart and John’s test is simple, namely love, and that the commands to believe and to love belong together and cannot be separated.

If our conscience itself accuses us within, because we are not doing our good works with the right intention, how can we hide our knowledge from Him to whom it is sung: Behold, Lord, you have known all things, and, Because the darkness will not be darkened from you, and the night will be illuminated like the day (Psalm 138)?
21: Says that seeing this love at work in us assures our hearts before God that we are of the truth.

If it truthfully answers us that we love, and that genuine love is in us, and not feigned, but sincere, seeking the brother’s salvation, expecting no gain from the brother except his salvation; likewise, if our heart does not reproach us, notably when we say in prayer: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors (Matthew VI), we have confidence towards God, not in the sight of men, but where God Himself sees in the heart.
22: The Conditions of Power in Prayer
Says obedience and love grow out of fellowship, which is the key to answered prayer, not a way of earning it.
Fellowship in God’s love means the assurance of answered prayer

This is a great and desirable promise given to the faithful. … For even if we do not always receive what we ask for in prayer to our will, yet we receive the reward of devotion for our salvation, just as the same Paul praying to the Lord received not what he sought, but what was useful for him.
23: Daily Study Bible · The Only Test · vv.19–24
Barclay says doubts come to every sensitive heart and John’s test is simple, namely love, and that the commands to believe and to love belong together and cannot be separated.

He placed the commandment in the singular number and subsequently added mandates to it, namely faith and love, because clearly these cannot be separated from each other. For neither can we rightly love one another without faith in Christ, nor can we truly believe in the name of Jesus Christ without fraternal love.
24: The Conditions of Power in Prayer

Let God therefore be your home, and be the home of God; abide in God, and let God abide in you. God abides in you to hold you, you abide in God so that you do not fall. Keep his commandments, hold onto charity.

1: Test the Spirits to See Whether They Are of God
Daily Study Bible · The Perils of the Surging Life of the Spirit · v.1
Barclay pictures the electric atmosphere of the early church, with so many spiritual manifestations that a test was needed, and says a spirit is from God when it takes its origin and life from him.

After John has completed his discourse on love for one's neighbor, and has demonstrated that this is a sign of the permanence of the Spirit we have received, he now adds a judgment concerning those who are truly brothers and neighbors, so that having this, we do not fall into the occasion of the commandment of love concerning false brothers, false apostles, and false prophets, bringing great harm upon ourselves from this.
2: Test the Spirits to See Whether They Are of God
Daily Study Bible · The Ultimate Heresy · vv.2–3
Barclay says John lays down two tests, that a spirit must acknowledge Jesus as the Messiah and as come in the flesh, and he calls the reality of Jesus’ manhood the most central thing in Christianity.

Confession in this place is understood not only as the Catholic faith but also as the good operation which is done through charity. Otherwise, some heretics confess, many schismatics, many false Catholics, that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, but they deny their confession by their deeds, not having charity.
3: Test the Spirits to See Whether They Are of God
Says true teaching presents a true Jesus, and that in John’s day the issue was whether Jesus had really come in a body of flesh and blood.
How to know when a false prophet speaks
He dissolves Jesus who denies either His divinity, or His soul, or His flesh, which the Catholic faith teaches that He truly has.
4: Test the Spirits to See Whether They Are of God
Says the child of God need not fear the spirit of antichrist, since the Spirit who dwells in believers is greater than he who is in the world.
The protection of the child of God

He thus teaches them to maintain humility, so that they do not attribute victory to their own strength, and are overcome by the arrogance of pride. He teaches them to always have confidence and hope of victory in the midst of adversities, retaining in their memory that the Lord is greater to protect than the devil to attack.
5: Test the Spirits to See Whether They Are of God
Daily Study Bible · The Cleavage Between the World and God · vv.4–6
Barclay says the Christian need not fear the heretic because Christ has won the victory, yet the false teachers will not listen, though Christ is always knocking at the door of every heart.

The Antichrists, that is, the heretics, even if they invoke the name of Christ or mark themselves with the sign of Christ, still they are from the world, that is, from the number of those who think worldly thoughts, who seek the lowly things, who are ignorant of celestial matters.
6: Test the Spirits to See Whether They Are of God
Says those who are of the world show it in their speech and are heard by the world, which does not reject them as it rejects God’s children.
The contrast between those in the world and those who are of God
In this, indeed, because he who listens to us has the Spirit of truth; he who does not listen to us has the spirit of error.
7: Love One Another for Love Is of God
Exclusivity: How Can There Be Just One True Religion?

For when he had shown whom one ought to love, namely those who are conformed in character, he adheres to what was said at the beginning, stating that both love and the one who loves are from God, and that only he who loves is born of God and knows God: while he who does not have love also does not know God, confirming opposites with opposites.
8: Love One Another for Love Is of God
Says we love one another because we are loved by God, not in order to earn his love.
What more could be said? God is charity. Therefore, to act against charity is to act against God.
9: Love One Another for Love Is of God
Exclusivity: How Can There Be Just One True Religion?
The Father's love is also proven in us, because he sent his only Son to die for us.
10: Love One Another for Love Is of God
We did not love him first. For he loved us to the extent that we might love him. Grace indeed goes before man, that he may love God, by which love he works good things.
11: Love One Another for Love Is of God

Not that we have loved Him, but that God did this, giving His Son for us, as if He ought to repay the beloved with an equal affection; but through love, first anticipating the benefit towards us, He sent His Son; and not only did He send Him, but also, for our sins, He was an atoning sacrifice by His own blood.
12: Daily Study Bible · Love Human and Divine · vv.7–21
Barclay takes love, human and divine, as the heart of the chapter, with God as love and Jesus as Son of God and Saviour of men, and closes on the presence of God in our lives.
Says no one has seen God the Father at any time, and that love is the evidence through which God is seen.
Seeing God through the evidence of love
But let no one think that this love, in which God abides, is preserved by a certain lax and lazy gentleness, indeed not by gentleness but by leniency and negligence.
13: God Abides in the One Who Loves and the One Who Confesses
Says believers can say we know, not merely hope, that they abide in God, and ties this assurance to the work of the Triune God in them.
Assurance of the work of the Triune God in us
This very thing, because He gave His Spirit to you, how do you know? Ask your own inner parts.
14: God Abides in the One Who Loves and the One Who Confesses
Daily Study Bible · Love Human and Divine · vv.7–21
Barclay takes love, human and divine, as the heart of the chapter, with God as love and Jesus as Son of God and Saviour of men, and closes on the presence of God in our lives.

Let no one despair of salvation, because although the diseases of crimes that weigh one down are great, the omnipotent physician has come to save. Yet let each remember that the same Son of God who came gently to save, will come sternly to judge.
15: God Abides in the One Who Loves and the One Who Confesses
Says believers can say we know, not merely hope, that they abide in God, and ties this assurance to the work of the Triune God in them.
Assurance of the work of the Triune God in us

He speaks of the perfect confession of the heart, which can neither be corrupted by the deceit of heretics who wrongly persuade, nor be shattered by the tortures of pagan persecutors, nor falter by the examples of fleshly brothers, nor waver by the sluggishness of one's own weakness.
16: God Abides in the One Who Loves and the One Who Confesses
He already said that above, behold he says it again. Love could not be commended to you more than by saying God. Perhaps you were going to scorn the gift of God: will you scorn God as well?
17: Daily Study Bible · Love Human and Divine · vv.7–21
Barclay takes love, human and divine, as the heart of the chapter, with God as love and Jesus as Son of God and Saviour of men, and closes on the presence of God in our lives.
Says love is perfected in the sense of being mature and complete, which gives boldness in the day of judgment.
The perfecting of love, both now and in eternity

Barclay says John turns to prayer for others, which must never be selfish, and explains the sin leading to death as the state of one who has listened to sin so long that he loves it and cannot repent.

Such is the diversity of sins, he says, that everything which deviates from the rule of equity is counted among the sins, although small sins cannot in any way take away or diminish the merit of righteousness from the just, as long as they are those without which this life cannot be lived, and likewise there are certain sins so discordant with all justice, committed with such iniquity, that without any contradiction, unless they are corrected, they lead their perpetrator to eternal punishment.
18: The grace of Christ, by which the faithful are reborn, preserves those who are called holy according to the purpose, so that they do not commit sin leading to death; and if they err in anything due to the frailty of human condition, it protects them from being touched by the malignant enemy.
